correctness.rationale: Read the frozen statement, proof and all supporting files. In deficit coordinates δ=1−x, v=y, the new deficit is nonnegative because (1−δ)e^δ≤1, and the new v is positive and at most v. Uniformly for 0≤δ≤Kv, the updates are δ′=av+O(v²) and v′=v+O(v²), so K>a gives δ′<Kv′ for sufficiently small v, including the δ=0 boundary. Since δ′≥av/2 in a smaller wedge, a positive limit of the nonincreasing v would eventually force a uniform contraction of v, a contradiction; v→0 and v′/v→1. Independently recovered the quadratic graph coefficient B=a²(d+1)/2 and reciprocal increment ad/2+[3a²d(d+1)/8]v+O(v²) from the formal expansion. This formal computation applies to actual wedge orbits: the graph H(v)=av+Bv² has defect O(v³), H(v) is inside the same wedge for sufficiently small v, and the transverse derivative of D−H(V) is O(v) between δ and H(v). For the scaled error |δ−H(v)|/v³ the resulting multiplicative coefficient is O(v)(v/v′)³→0 and the forcing is bounded, so it remains bounded. This yields a controlled fourth-order remainder for the cubic v update, not just a formal center graph. Positive reciprocal increments in the limit give 1/v_n∼(ad/2)n; one further summation gives 1/v_n=(ad/2)n+O(log n). Substituting back leaves an absolutely summable O(log n/n²) increment error after removing the linear term and (3a(d+1)/4)/n. The harmonic sum minus log n converges, proving the finite orbit-dependent constant and the unavoidable positive coefficient. The uploaded SymPy checker and numerical diagnostics were read, not run.

value.rationale: A reciprocal decay rate at neutral invasion is a natural deterministic timing observable for this published map. The exact logarithmic drift is detectable beyond the leading algebraic law and cannot be tuned away by a change of initial state. The finite orbit-dependent correction is proved on an entire positive invariant wedge rather than a formal center curve. The general iteration device is standard; the value is the controlled coefficient and range of validity for this specific nonlinear threshold, not general or empirical ecological significance.
